page: Hetzner Cloud ccx13 is a general-purpose cloud instance provisioned with dedicated compute resources. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the server features an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, and SHA-NI, while AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent.

System memory consists of 8.0 GB of RAM, equating to roughly 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is locally bundled, comprising an 80 GB NVMe SSD, while dedicated GPU hardware is not included. The platform operates on QEMU virtualization and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring reliance on IPv6 or separately assigned networking.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-threaded performance contrasted with low overall parallel throughput due to the single-core configuration. In stress-ng, single-core execution reached a score of 3074.79, placing it in the upper quartile, yet multi-core performance mirrored this exact figure and landed in the bottom quartile. Geekbench scores follow a similar pattern, registering 1940.0 in single-core and 2469.0 in multi-core testing. Memory performance tests showed read bandwidth of 32.42 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 26.66 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB blocks, accompanied by lower comparative marks in PassMark database operations and Redis SET throughput (2.8 million operations per second). Small-model language inference for a 135M model achieved 95.1 tokens per second during generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ccx13 provides guaranteed, unshared CPU capacity without noisy-neighbor contention at an entry-level capacity point. The low core count limits total aggregate throughput for parallel compilation, heavy database operations, and high-concurrency web serving. As a result, the instance is best suited for lightweight production services, single-threaded processing tasks, background workers, staging systems, and low-traffic web applications that require steady CPU execution.
